script: Spread and total were not saved for PIT at CLE, so the Week 4 script is inferred only from PIT and CLE three-game form. PIT has been Jaylen Warren at 38 carries for 216 rush yards plus 14 targets for 110 receiving yards, with Pat Freiermuth at 14 targets for 108 yards, while DK Metcalf's 24 targets and 339 air yards produced only 98 receiving yards. CLE has been Deshaun Watson at 20 carries for 109 rush yards and Denzel Boston at 16 targets for 195 yards and 225 air yards, while Quinshon Judkins has 42 carries for 124 yards at 2.95 YPC.
who_goes_off: PIT's Jaylen Warren should stay the engine against CLE's run defense allowing 4.67 YPC and 13 runs of 10-plus, after Warren's 216 rush yards and 110 receiving yards. PIT tight end Pat Freiermuth (108 yards on 14 targets, 118 air yards) is the pass fit because CLE allows 9.44 YPA in the middle versus 6.32 left and 6.44 right. CLE's Denzel Boston is the explosive receiver at 195 yards and 225 air yards on 16 targets into a PIT defense allowing 8.15 YPA left, 8.0 right, and 11 passes of 20-plus on 89 attempts.
weak_spot: CLE's real weak spot is the middle at 9.44 YPA on 18 attempts, not the outside at 6.32 left on 47 attempts and 6.44 right on 39 attempts, and CLE also allows 4.67 rush YPC with 13 runs of 10-plus. PIT's weak spot is the perimeter: left 8.15 YPA on 34 attempts and right 8.0 on 28 attempts versus a tighter middle at 6.95 on 19 attempts, with 11 passes of 20-plus on 89 attempts and 4.56 rush YPC allowed.
injury_fallout: No injury report was saved for PIT or CLE, so no absence shifts PIT targets off DK Metcalf's 24 or onto CLE's Jerry Jeudy at 5 targets for 26 yards. PIT and CLE usage is taken as listed: Jaylen Warren 38 carries, Quinshon Judkins 42 carries, and Deshaun Watson 20 carries.
qb_vs_blitz: PIT quarterback Aaron Rodgers is -0.40 EPA per dropback versus the blitz on 30 dropbacks and -0.17 with no blitz, and CLE blitzes only 20%, so PIT does not get an unblitzed EPA spike. CLE quarterback Deshaun Watson is -0.04 EPA versus the blitz on 39 dropbacks and +0.17 with no blitz, and PIT's 27% blitz rate is the look that flattens Watson and pushes more CLE value into his 109 rush yards on 20 carries.

picks.why: PIT's Pat Freiermuth is at 108 receiving yards on 14 targets and 118 air yards (36.0 per game) versus a 27.5 line, and that TE usage attacks CLE's middle hole of 9.44 YPA on 18 attempts rather than CLE's tighter 6.32 left and 6.44 right.

PIT's DK Metcalf has 98 receiving yards on 24 targets and 339 air yards (32.7 per game) against a 46.5 line, and CLE's perimeter holds opponents to 6.32 YPA left and 6.44 right while Rodgers is still -0.17 EPA with no blitz and CLE blitzes only 20%.
